items.headline: Planning Commission agenda lists 316 apartments at the 400 Saratoga Avenue golf course
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a recommendation on a General Plan amendment and rezoning for a five-story, 316-unit apartment building at 400 Saratoga Avenue. The project would also reconfigure the existing nine-hole golf course and dedicate land for a public park. An Environmental Impact Report was prepared for the project.

items.headline: Townhomes and duplex with commercial space proposed near Civic Center Drive
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a vesting tentative subdivision map for condominium purposes covering 14 townhomes and a duplex building with commercial space at 860 and 858 Civic Center Drive and 1526 Alviso Street. The agenda cited a CEQA exemption under AB 130 (2025).

items.headline: Planning Commission agenda lists neighbor's appeal of Rita Court home addition
items.summary: The November 18 agenda listed an appeal of the Development Review Officer's approval of an addition at 2261 Rita Court. The proposal calls for adding 517 square feet on the first floor and 1,000 square feet on a new second floor. The existing single-story home sits on a 6,272-square-foot lot.

items.headline: Gymnastics facility proposed in Corvin Drive warehouse
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a conditional use permit to allow a gymnastics facility in 7,116 square feet of an existing 16,576-square-foot warehouse at 3051 Corvin Drive.

items.headline: 69-stall parking lot proposed at 2740 Scott Boulevard after demolition
items.summary: The November 18 Planning Commission agenda listed a conditional use permit for a 69-stall surface parking lot at 2740 Scott Boulevard. It also listed an architectural review to allow complete demolition of the existing vacant structures and a minor use permit for off-site parking.

items.headline: Council agenda: pause on data center and large energy-use approvals
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed an item titled "Pause on Data Center and Large Energy Use Project Approvals and Develop Urgency Ordinances." The title points to a temporary halt on approving data centers and other large energy-use projects while the city drafts urgency ordinances.

items.headline: Council closed-session agenda lists YIMBY and Chen lawsuits against Cupertino
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed a closed session on existing litigation involving two Santa Clara County Superior Court cases: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino, et al., and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino, et al. The agenda names the cases but does not describe the claims.

items.headline: Council agenda includes ordinance to change councilmember pay
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed consideration of an ordinance amending Cupertino Municipal Code Section 2.16.020 on City Council compensation. The same agenda listed amendments to the Council Procedures Manual, an item postponed from May 5, 2026.
